text.f4: His video has to do it in under a second.
text.l2: A new street, far from his balcony.
text.l3: And she is waiting for his video.
text.p2: The video is chopped into fifteen hundred small packets,
text.p4: Radio waves carry them to the nearest cell tower.
text.u1: From the tower, they dive under the street,
text.u2: into a glass cable, as flashes of light.
text.r2: and passes the packet one step closer.
text.r3: If one road is jammed, it picks another.
text.s2: So the cable keeps going, straight into the sea.
text.b1: Three kilometres down, in the dark,
text.b2: the light races along the sea floor,
text.b3: at two hundred thousand kilometres a second.
text.e1: The light fades on the way,
text.e2: so a repeater boosts it, every sixty to a hundred kilometres.
text.c1: And the cable? About as thick as a garden hose.
text.c2: Steel, plastic and copper, layer on layer,
text.c3: all to protect a few glass fibres,
text.c4: each as thin as a human hair.
text.g1: Our packet crosses the Arabian Sea, the Red Sea, the Mediterranean, and reaches London.
text.g2: More than ninety-five percent of data between continents travels this way.
text.n1: All fifteen hundred packets reach her phone in a blink.
